name: Skyworks Solutions, Inc.

profile.description: Skyworks Solutions designs, manufactures, and markets analog and mixed-signal semiconductor products for mobile, automotive, broadband, IoT, and industrial applications. The company's front-end modules, amplifiers, filters, and switches are critical components in 5G smartphones, Wi-Fi 7 routers, automotive connectivity, and data center infrastructure. Founded in 1962 and headquartered in Irvine, California, with approximately $9.4B market cap.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Skyworks secured a multi-generational Android OEM design win in Q2 FY2026 with expected revenue exceeding $1 billion through 2030, representing a significant new customer commitment [1]. Broad Markets delivered its 9th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY growth driven by Wi-Fi 7, data center connectivity, and automotive infotainment programs, diversifying the company beyond smartphone RF dependence [1]. However, overall revenue remains below FY2021 peak of $5.1B, with Q2 FY2026 at $943.7M down 1% YoY [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Skyworks is shipping connectivity components that enable AI infrastructure — data center networking, edge IoT, and automotive computing — making the company an AI-enabling supplier [1]. CIO Satya Jayadev has discussed using AI internally as a 'force multiplier,' aiming for one engineer to do the work of four through agentic AI tools [2]. No specific quantified AI revenue or savings disclosed. Market Share (1/2): Skyworks holds a strong position in mobile RF front-end modules as a major Apple supplier and is gaining share in Wi-Fi 7 enterprise and consumer markets, with automotive infotainment engagements secured with major manufacturers [1]. However, Qualcomm's integrated modem-RF strategy and Apple's in-house modem development create competitive pressure. Pipeline (1/2): Wi-Fi 7 product ramp advancing with enterprise and consumer partners, multi-generational Android OEM design win providing revenue visibility through 2030, and Broad Markets expected to reach approximately 43% of total sales in Q3 FY2026 [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Skyworks invests significantly in RF semiconductor R&D across multiple technology nodes and application domains, with proprietary filter technology, GaAs and SiGe process capabilities, and integrated front-end solutions [1].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Skyworks' purpose centers on 'connecting everyone and everything, all the time' through semiconductor solutions — clear and relevant but broadly shared across the connectivity semiconductor industry [2]. New CEO Philip Brace (appointed February 2025) has emphasized accountability and execution but hasn't yet articulated a distinctive vision beyond operational improvement. Community Impact (1/2): Skyworks has reduced gross Scope 1+2 CO2e emissions by 42% (51,592 tons) from factory operations since 2018, with targets for 30% reduction by 2030 and net-zero by 2050 aligned with the Paris Agreement [3]. The company recently removed supermajority voting requirements from its charter in response to investor governance proposals [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): Skyworks employs approximately 10,000 people with generally stable operations across global manufacturing facilities [2]. The CEO transition from long-tenured Liam Griffin to Philip Brace in February 2025 introduces leadership uncertainty, and Comparably rates the executive team C+, suggesting average employee sentiment [2]. No specific retention or turnover data available. Insider Buying (0/2): No significant net insider buying identified in the last 12 months [4]. The company returns capital primarily through dividends ($106.8M quarterly) and modest share repurchases ($7.5M in Q2 FY2026) [1].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Skyworks' balance sheet is a standout strength with D/E of just 17.3% ($996.6M debt against $1,436M cash and marketable securities), well below the 70% target [1]. Forward P/E of 12.89 is deeply discounted, reflecting depressed current earnings with expected recovery [4]. The dividend profile is strong — 12 consecutive years of growth with 9.1% 5yr CAGR and current yield of 4.54% — but the GAAP payout ratio of approximately 117% is unsustainable on current earnings and scores 0 on that metric [4]. ROE of 6.3% reflects the earnings trough, well below the 15% target [4]. Profit margin of 8.9% has compressed from historical 20%+ levels as GAAP results are burdened by amortization and restructuring charges [1]. Revenue growth is negative at -1.0% for Q2 FY2026 with 5yr CAGR near 0% from peak FY2021 levels [4]. Liquidity floor easily cleared: 6.22M avg daily volume at $62.56 = $389M [4].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Skyworks' analog and mixed-signal semiconductors are physical components that AI structurally cannot replace — RF front-end modules, power amplifiers, and filters require specialized semiconductor fabrication and physical-layer signal processing that exists entirely outside AI's domain [1]. AI infrastructure growth actively increases demand for Skyworks' products: data centers require more high-speed connectivity components, edge IoT devices need robust wireless capability, and autonomous vehicles demand automotive-grade RF solutions [1]. The Broad Markets segment's double-digit growth driven by data center and edge IoT programs validates this thesis. However, Apple's in-house modem development creates a customer-specific risk (not an AI risk per se), and integrated solutions from Qualcomm could reduce RF content per device in future smartphone designs. Analysts view Skyworks as an AI beneficiary through infrastructure enablement, not an AI disruption target [2]. AI Opportunity (1/1): Skyworks generates meaningful revenue from AI-adjacent applications — data center connectivity components, Wi-Fi 7 modules for AI edge devices, and automotive computing connectivity. Broad Markets segment delivered double-digit YoY growth for the 9th consecutive quarter, driven partly by AI data center infrastructure demand [1].

infinite_game.summary: Skyworks demonstrates mixed infinite game characteristics. The company has endured for 64 years through multiple semiconductor industry cycles, and the Broad Markets diversification represents forward-looking strategy. However, the generic connectivity mission lacks Just Cause distinctiveness, the new CEO hasn't yet established long-term vision, and the company's heavy Apple dependence created a fragility that the multi-generational Android OEM design win is only beginning to address.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Connecting everyone and everything, all the time' through semiconductor innovation is a valid purpose but lacks distinctiveness — it could describe any connectivity chipmaker from Qualcomm to Broadcom [2]. The company has operated since 1962 (64 years), demonstrating endurance, but the purpose has not been the competitive advantage driving transformative strategic decisions. Skyworks' success is attributable to engineering execution and customer intimacy with Apple rather than a transcendent cause. The CEO transition to Philip Brace has not yet produced a refreshed vision beyond operational improvement.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Skyworks employs approximately 10,000 people with generally stable operations across global manufacturing facilities in the US, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore [2]. The February 2025 CEO transition from long-tenured Liam Griffin to Philip Brace was executed without major organizational disruption, suggesting institutional stability. Comparably rates the executive team C+, indicating average employee sentiment toward leadership [2]. Brace has emphasized a 'no-blame' culture around lost customer sockets, which signals some trust-building intent. No major layoffs or cultural controversies identified.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Skyworks demonstrates competitive awareness that drives self-improvement. The multi-generational Android OEM design win directly responds to Qualcomm's integrated modem-RF strategy by proving Skyworks can deliver competitive RF solutions for non-Apple OEMs [1]. The expansion into Wi-Fi 7 reflects learning from Broadcom's Wi-Fi dominance, and the data center push responds to the competitive landscape's AI-driven demand shift. Management's competitive language focuses on 'winning designs' through superior technology rather than destroying rivals [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Skyworks has gradually evolved from a pure mobile RF supplier (historically 70%+ of revenue from smartphones) to a diversified analog semiconductor company, with Broad Markets now approaching 43% of total sales [1]. This diversification away from smartphone dependence is meaningful and deliberate, driven by recognition that Apple customer concentration was an existential risk. However, the transformation has been incremental over many years rather than a dramatic strategic pivot — the company hasn't fundamentally reinvented its business model, technology base, or market approach.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Skyworks committed to a multi-generational Android OEM design win requiring significant upfront investment for $1B+ in revenue through 2030, demonstrating willingness to bet on long-term customer relationships [1]. The company maintained its dividend through the earnings downturn (12 consecutive years of growth) even as the GAAP payout ratio exceeded 100%, showing commitment to shareholder returns over short-term balance sheet optimization [4]. The Broad Markets investment during a period of mobile revenue decline represents choosing diversification over cost-cutting. However, these decisions lack the transformative boldness of truly courageous leadership — they are sensible strategic moves rather than painful sacrifices.

investment_thesis: Skyworks offers deep value in semiconductors with a forward P/E of just 12.89x, a 4.54% dividend yield backed by 12 consecutive years of growth, and a fortress balance sheet with $1.44B cash against $997M debt (D/E of 17.3%) [1][4]. Q2 FY2026 revenue of $943.7M included a landmark multi-generational Android OEM design win expected to generate over $1 billion through 2030, providing long-term revenue visibility beyond the Apple relationship [1]. Broad Markets delivered its 9th consecutive quarter of double-digit YoY growth driven by Wi-Fi 7, data center, and automotive, now approaching 43% of total sales [1]. Q3 FY2026 guidance of $900-950M with Broad Markets at approximately 43% suggests the diversification strategy is accelerating. The non-GAAP operating margin of 20% demonstrates underlying profitability that the GAAP figures (burdened by amortization) obscure [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on structural mobile revenue decline and earnings quality concerns. Q2 FY2026 revenue declined 1% YoY and GAAP net income fell 48.2% to $35.6M, with GAAP operating margin at just 4.5% versus 20% non-GAAP — a $147M gap driven by amortization, restructuring, and stock-based compensation [1]. Free cash flow was negative $32M in Q2 due to elevated capex of $82.3M, and operating cash flow plunged 87.7% YoY from $409.5M to $50.3M [1]. The GAAP payout ratio of 117% is unsustainable — the $106.8M quarterly dividend exceeds GAAP earnings, and a dividend cut would remove the yield support thesis and trigger institutional selling [4]. Apple modem internalization remains the paramount risk: Apple designing its own cellular modems could progressively reduce Skyworks' RF content per iPhone, threatening the company's largest customer relationship. The 5yr revenue CAGR near 0% from FY2021 peak of $5.1B suggests the mobile RF market may be structurally declining for discrete component suppliers [4].
key_catalysts: Multi-generational Android OEM design win generating $1B+ revenue through 2030 diversifies customer concentration away from Apple and validates Skyworks' competitive position in non-Apple RF markets [1]

Broad Markets approaching 43% of revenue with 9 consecutive quarters of double-digit growth, driven by Wi-Fi 7, data center AI infrastructure, and automotive connectivity — potential to become the majority revenue source within 2 years [1]
Forward P/E of 12.89x with 4.54% dividend yield creates compelling value if earnings stabilize around non-GAAP guidance levels, offering 30-50% upside to historical mid-teens P/E multiples [4]
key_risks: Apple modem internalization — Apple designing its own cellular modems would progressively reduce Skyworks' RF content per iPhone, threatening the company's largest single-customer revenue stream and potentially accelerating mobile revenue decline [1]

Dividend sustainability — GAAP payout ratio of 117% is unsustainable, and negative free cash flow of -$32M in Q2 FY2026 means the $427M annual dividend is being partially funded from the balance sheet rather than operations [1][4]

GAAP vs non-GAAP divergence — the $147M quarterly gap between GAAP and non-GAAP operating income raises questions about underlying earnings quality, as amortization, restructuring, and SBC represent real economic costs [1]
